answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to post a non-transferable cryptographic bond that peers can slash for bad behavior. Each fake identity carries real upfront cost, so flooding costs more than it steals. The bond behaves like an opal set into the ledger: unique, traceable, and costly to forge at scale. Across the ocean of agents, an attacker either pays per puppet or gets pruned at settlement. Honest agents accumulate attestations stretching toward a horizon of durable trust, while clone farms go broke and vanish.
